ordered_diagnoses: Plakophilin-2 Mutation-Related Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy

s1.syndrome_frame: Intermittent palpitations with worsening over the previous hour, characterized by wide complex tachycardia and abnormal cardiac structure and function
salient_findings: Wide complex tachycardia at rate of 190 bpm
Grossly dilated RV with high RV end diastolic volume
key_facts: Male patient in his 20s
Complaints of intermittent palpitations for 2 days
Worsening of palpitations in the previous hour
No history of chest pain, dyspnea, congestion, or fever
No past cardiac history or family history of similar complaints
Blood pressure was 110/72 mm Hg
Respiratory rate was 14 bpm
ECG showed wide complex tachycardia with atypical left bundle branch morphology
QRS duration of 146 ms with no evidence of AV dissociation
Echocardiography showed global hypokinesia of right ventricle and dilated RV
Cardiac MRI showed grossly dilated RV and high RV end diastolic volume
Postcontrast hyperenhancement along RV free wall and other areas

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG, echocardiography, and cardiac MRI results all point towards a diagnosis of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy, with evidence of global hypokinesia of the right ventricle, dilated RV, and postcontrast hyperenhancement along the RV free wall, which are characteristic findings of this condition.

rejected.label: Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Tachycardia
rejected.why: While the patient presented with tachycardia, the imaging findings suggest a more structural issue with the right ventricle rather than a focal source of tachycardia in the outflow tract.

rejected.label: Ventricular Tachycardia
rejected.why: Ventricular tachycardia is a broader term that encompasses various conditions, but the specific findings in this case point towards a more specific diagnosis of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Plakophilin-2 Mutation-Related Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While this could be a possible underlying cause, there is no specific information provided about a Plakophilin-2 mutation, making it less directly supported by the case facts than Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Catecholaminergic Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a history of stress or emotional events triggering arrhythmias, which is not mentioned in the case, and the structural abnormalities seen in the imaging studies are not characteristic of this condition.
